Note::TexAccessor::add_math_delimiters¶

Back to Note Tex Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::TexAccessor::add_math_delimiters() const

Make Each Cell A Complete Math Fragment¶

add_math_delimiters() returns a shape-preserving Text Note in which every non-empty cell has one complete outer math delimiter pair. Use it when each cell is an expression that must be embedded independently in TeX source. It does not decide whether prose is mathematical; the caller makes that semantic choice by selecting this operation.

Plain text is trimmed of surrounding ASCII whitespace and wrapped in $...$. Cells already enclosed by $...$, $$...$$, \(...\), or \[...\] retain their delimiter style. A one-sided outer delimiter is completed rather than wrapped again. Empty or whitespace-only cells become "", not "$$".

The method is idempotent: applying it to its own output produces the same values. It operates cell by cell, preserves rank and every extent, and allocates fresh Text storage. Undefined propagates. Bytes and native Bool, Int64, or Float64 Notes reject because no implicit decoding or formatting is performed. Work is linear in the total input bytes.

This is lexical wrapping, not TeX validation. It does not parse an expression, check command names, or repair delimiters nested inside a cell. Use balance_math_delims() when an authored fragment’s internal outer delimiters may be incomplete.

Example 1: Plain, Complete, Partial, And Empty Cells¶

const auto expressions = pluss::make_note(
    {" x+y ", "$z$", R"(\(a+b\))", R"(\[c=d\])", "", "$u", R"(v\))"});
std::cout << expressions.tex().add_math_delimiters() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[7], dim=1, numel=7, encoding=utf8)
["$x+y$", "$z$", "\\(a+b\\)", "\\[c=d\\]", "", "$u$", "\\(v\\)"]

The existing delimiter convention is preserved; only the plain expression chooses the default dollar pair.

Example 2: Matrix Geometry Is Preserved¶

const auto grid = pluss::make_note(
    std::vector<std::string>{"a", "b", "$c$", ""},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
std::cout << grid.tex().add_math_delimiters() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["$a$", "$b$"], 
  ["$c$", ""]
]

Example 3: Undefined Propagates¶

std::cout << std::boolalpha << "undefined="
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().add_math_delimiters().defined()
          << '\n';

Output¶

undefined=false

Example 4: Native Numeric Storage Is Not Stringified¶

try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 2})
      .tex().add_math_delimiters();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "Int64 add delimiters: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

Int64 add delimiters: rejected

See Also¶

  • balance_math_delims: repair unmatched outer math delimiters.

  • escape: protect literal text rather than marking it as mathematics.

  • wrap_inline_math and wrap_display_math: request a particular delimiter spelling.
